script.problem: It reuses a line from the Prep cards word for word.

terra.problem: The passage does not say the Israelites already keep the animals with them.
The passage does not place the Tent of Meeting in the camp.
Aaron being Moses's brother is a fact from outside the passage and needs a reference.
The priests do not simply take over after the man brings the animal. He also slaughters, skins and cuts it.
Aaron being Moses's brother is a fact from outside the passage and needs a reference.
Saying the burnt offering goes up whole can suggest the animal is not cut up. The animal is skinned and cut into pieces.
The peace offering does not have a fat-only rule. The kidneys and the lobe of the liver are also included.
The explanation repeats the list several times without adding a distinct thought or much of Papa Dorin's personality.
The middle of the explanation simply repeats that the two named birds are the two on the list. It feels generic rather than like Papa Dorin.
The priest, not the man bringing the offering, tears the bird open.
Aaron being Moses's brother is a fact from outside the passage and needs a reference.
Aaron being Moses's brother is a fact from outside the passage and needs a reference.
Aaron being Moses's brother is a fact from outside the passage and needs a reference.
The fine flour and oil are common to the offerings, but saying the recipe does not change overlooks the different preparations.
The text prohibits leaven in grain offerings, but it does not explicitly say that is why the cakes and wafers were unleavened.
The passage says honey must not be burned as a food offering and must not go up on the altar as a pleasing aroma. The blanket statement that it cannot go on the altar fire goes beyond that wording.
The final sentence omits the text's qualification that leaven and honey must not go up on the altar as a pleasing aroma.
The final sentence turns the restriction into a blanket ban from the altar, omitting the text's qualification about a pleasing aroma.
The text does not specify that the oil and frankincense are added after roasting.
Saying it follows the same pattern as the others suggests all the other grain offerings include frankincense, which the passage does not say.
Aaron being Moses's brother is a fact from outside the passage and needs a reference.
The closing line about a list being easy to remember after hearing it a few times is generic and adds no useful insight or personality.
The explanation asserts where the baker's mix-up came from, though Papa Dorin has not been told the baker's reasoning.
Calling the burnt offering the whole animal overlooks that its skin is removed before the rest is burned.
The explanation says grain is still on the baker's mind, though Papa Dorin cannot know that.
